pages.title: Fundamental CTS Data Types and Variables in C#
pages.content:
### Value Types and the Common Type System (CTS)

In C#, every data type maps directly to a underlying .NET Common Type System (CTS) type:

| C# Alias | CTS Type | Size | Range / Purpose |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `int` | `System.Int32` | 32 bits | -2,147,483,648 to 2,147,483,647 |
| `long` | `System.Int64` | 64 bits | -9 x 10^18 to 9 x 10^18 (suffix `L`) |
| `float` | `System.Single` | 32 bits | 7 decimal digits precision (suffix `f`) |
| `double` | `System.Double` | 64 bits | 15-17 decimal digits precision (default for decimals) |
| `decimal`| `System.Decimal`| 128 bits| 28-29 digits precision (suffix `m`, financial math) |
| `bool` | `System.Boolean`| 8 bits | `true` or `false` |
| `char` | `System.Char` | 16 bits | Single UTF-16 character in single quotes `'A'` |

#### Implicit Typing with `var`
The `var` keyword instructs the compiler to infer the type at compile-time: `var score = 100;` (inferred as `int`). It remains strictly typed and cannot change type later.

callout.title: Decimal for Currency
callout.text: Always use the decimal type (suffix m) for monetary calculations in C# to eliminate floating-point rounding inaccuracies.

checkpoint.question: Which numeric data type in C# is best suited for financial and monetary calculations requiring high precision?
checkpoint.explanation: The decimal type provides 128-bit precision with base-10 representation, eliminating binary rounding errors inherent in float and double.

msa.title: Module Assessment: Variables and Data Types

questions.question: What is the difference between Value Types and Reference Types in C#?
options: Value types store their data directly (typically on the stack), while reference types store a reference to data on the managed heap
Reference types are destroyed as soon as they are declared
Value types are allocated only by the garbage collector
questions.explanation: Value types (int, double, struct, enum) hold their data directly in their storage location. Reference types (string, class, array) hold a pointer to heap memory managed by the GC.

questions.question: Which literal suffix denotes a decimal value in C#?
questions.explanation: In C#, the 'm' or 'M' suffix designates a decimal literal (e.g. 19.95m). Without a suffix, a floating-point literal defaults to double.

questions.question: Can an integer be implicitly used as a boolean condition (e.g., `if (count)`) in C#?
options: No, C# is strictly type-safe and requires a boolean expression evaluating to true or false
Yes, 0 is false and any non-zero integer is true
Yes, but only in release builds
Yes, if using the var keyword
questions.explanation: Unlike C and C++, C# enforces strict type safety: conditionals in if, while, etc. must evaluate to an explicit bool type.

questions.question: What is true about the `var` keyword in C#?
options: It is strongly typed; the compiler determines the type at compile-time and it cannot be changed afterwards
It creates a dynamic variable that can change types at runtime
It is an alias for System.Object
It can only be used with strings
questions.explanation: var provides compile-time type inference. Once inferred, the variable is permanently and strictly bound to that type.

questions.question: What is the default value of an uninitialized local variable in a C# method?
options: C# compiler requires local variables to be explicitly assigned before use; accessing an unassigned local variable causes a compilation error
0 for numbers and null for objects
questions.explanation: C# enforces definite assignment analysis: local variables must be explicitly assigned a value before their value can be read, or the compiler reports CS0165.

questions.question: Which block keyword in C# enables runtime overflow checking for integral-type arithmetic operations?
questions.explanation: The checked keyword instructs the runtime to throw an OverflowException if an integral arithmetic operation exceeds the bounds of the destination type.

questions.question: What is the size of the `char` type in C#?
questions.explanation: In C#, char represents a 16-bit Unicode UTF-16 code unit.

questions.question: How do you declare a constant variable whose value cannot be modified after compilation?
questions.explanation: The const keyword declares compile-time constants whose values are burned directly into IL metadata.

questions.question: What is boxing in C#?
options: Converting a value type instance into an object reference type on the managed heap
Converting a reference type to a value type
Wrapping an integer into an array
Compressing memory in the garbage collector
questions.explanation: Boxing is the process of converting a value type to System.Object or any interface type implemented by this value type, allocating a heap wrapper.

questions.question: What is the result of casting a double with value 9.87 to an int: `int x = (int)9.87;`?
questions.explanation: Explicit casting from floating-point types to integral types in C# truncates the fractional portion towards zero.
